title: Correct final speed
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (1) must be 3 m/s.

title: Correct final force
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (2) must be 12800 N.

title: Total force calculation
description: Important: The solution must correctly sum the four external forces to find the total upward force of 1800 N.

title: Work-energy for launch
description: Important: For part (1), the solution must apply the work-energy theorem from launch to the moment the force stops, equating the work done by the total force to the gain in kinetic energy.

title: Work-energy for impact
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must apply the work-energy theorem during the impact, considering work done by gravity and the average impact force over the stopping distance h2.

title: Sign error in impact
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly assigns signs to the work done by the impact force or gravity during the stopping phase.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The solution should correctly convert heights from cm to m for use in energy calculations.

title: Force direction clarity
description: Optional: The solution clearly distinguishes between the force on the object by the ground and the force on the ground by the object (Newton's third law).
